exam_suitability.notes: Five 1-point parts fit the short-FRQ grain, the load is low and no calculator is needed.

difficulty.label: exam_prep
difficulty.rationale: Standard FRQ-style item on one comparative-statics chain: lower interest rates reduce foreign demand for the ket and raise supply of the ket. The ket depreciates, net exports rise, and real GDP rises. Students must draw a labeled FX graph, shift the curves, and explain the capital-flow reasoning and the net export/GDP link. Concept depth is moderate and every part is routine for the unit. There is no computation and the stimulus is short. The only wording issue is that the stimulus is sparse, but the fixed interest-rate-to-capital-flow model is clearly intended. The graph-drawing, shifting and verbal explanation make it more demanding than basic recall, but not advanced.
